WARM-UP

Basketball School

I-ON-I CHANGE OF SPEED

10 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available space (no baskets needed). Players line-up across the sideline of each full-court available.

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per player

### DESCRIPTION

Players will begin without balls in groups of two. One player is designated as the lead and the other player is the shadow. Players must stay in a straight line between each sideline. The lead has 20 seconds to repeat different movements, being as creative as they can. The shadow must attempt to replicate the leads' movements. Change roles after 20 seconds.

### SCORING

1 point for creating separation.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Developing ball manipulation skills
- Exploring various functional movements

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Add a dribble. The lead must attempt to gain more than an arm's distance of separation. Players can move forwards and backwards. Each time this occurs, they gain 1 point.
- The shadow must remain on the side of the offensive player the whole time.
- Move away from the sideline to use every available basket. The lead starts at half-court, walking towards the basket while dribbling. The moment they change speed and sprint; it becomes a live 1-on-1.

### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure players remain in a straight line for the prior activities to avoid collisions.
- Encourage players to be creative exploring different movements as part of their warm-up.

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How many different ways can you move?"
- "How can you disguise your change of speed?"

WARM-UP

Basketball School

3-ON-2 PASS TRIANGLE

10 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available space (no baskets needed)

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball, 3 cones per group

### DESCRIPTION

A triangle will be set-up in the available spaces around the court, with three players standing over the cones and two defenders in the middle. The passers must keep possession of the ball as long as possible. A defender can steal a passer's spot by stealing the ball, deflecting a pass, or forcing an off-target pass (a pass where a teammate has to move to catch the ball).

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Make the space slightly bigger to give the passers more time on the ball.
- Players must take a dribble on every catch and only pass with one hand.
- Passers are allowed to move inside the triangle as opposed to staying at the bases. They attempt to complete eight passes in a row maintaining possession of the ball.

### SCORING

N/A

### STAFF ROLE

- Help players set up the triangles.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Ball movement
- Reading defense and identifying open players
- Faking a pass then making a pass

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "Can you find an open teammate?"
- "How can you make a lead to get open within the 3-on-2 keep-away?"

GAME TIME

Basketball School

## GAME TIME

is where players participate in different activities and games designed to stimulate their growth and development.

These activities have been carefully created to mimic the game of basketball. With the NBA Basketball School Camp Curriculum, players develop technically and tactically through the actual act of playing basketball itself.

Each Game Time activity is clearly described and presented in the following format: name, time, space, equipment, description, scoring, types of loads, staff roles, key concepts, and guiding questions. Coaches are encouraged to utilize the information presented and to expand on those ideas in a way that would be most meaningful to their players.

GAME TIME

Basketball School

2-ON-1 HALF-COURT

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

### DESCRIPTION

Two players will begin on offense with one ball in a random location along the half-court line (close together, far apart, medium distance apart, etc.). This should be different every time. The defender can start in any random location outside of the 3PT area. As soon as the offense moves off the half-court line, they have a five second shot clock to score a lay-up at the rim.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Start closer to the basket (e.g. on the 3PT line instead of the half-court line).
- One offensive player must begin on a sideline while the other begins on the half-court line. The defender starts in any location inside the 3PT line but outside the paint. Play the 2-on-1 with the same rules.
- Add a +1 trailing defender to play 2-on-1+1. The +1 defender stands five steps behind the offensive player with the ball.

### SCORING

Offensive team will get 2 points for made baskets.

### STAFF ROLE

- Help the players explore the varied spacing locations.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Creating space and keeping advantage
- Scanning and reading the defense
- Shot selection
- Creative finishing
- Stunting and recovering defensively

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "Who is more open - you or your teammate?"
- "As the defender, how can you position yourself to guard both players and prioritize protecting the basket?"

GAME TIME

Basketball School

I-ON-I CREATE AN ADVANTAGE

IG MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group.

### DESCRIPTION

Players will start their 1-on-1 in a neutral position with the defense positioned directly in front of the offense, in any location inside the 3PT line but outside the paint. The defense begins with the ball and hands it over to the offense to start a live 1-on-1. From this moment, the offense has three dribbles to score inside the smile. Only two games of 1-on-1 can take place simultaneously on each basket.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- If too difficult for younger players, the defender can only use 1 hand and must stand to the right or left of the offensive player to start the 1-on-1.
- The offense starts outside the 3PT line.
- Add a +1 defender who can play defense but is not allowed to move. They can stunt at the ball based on where they position themselves.

### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points for made baskets.

### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure only two games of 1-on-1 occur simultaneously.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Creating an advantage against neutral
- Containing the ball defensively

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How can you pressure the ball aggressively without allowing the offense to easily drive past you?"

GAME TIME

Basketball School

3-ON-3, SCORE THROUGH A 1-ON-1

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

### DESCRIPTION

Three offensive players will space in varied locations outside the 3PT line with three defenders guarding them and a team of three waiting along the baseline. The offense has a 14 second shot clock to score. If the defense gains possession (defensive rebound or forced turnover), they must clear the ball before the shot clock starts again. On a score, the team that gets scored on rotates off, while the new team sprints onto defense. Players can only score through a 1-on-1 from the perimeter or a 1-on-1 post-up. Any other score (e.g. pass and cut, pick and roll, off-ball screen, dribble hand-off, etc.) does not count.

### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Driving and kicking the ball if second help defender is activated
- Creating space and keeping advantage

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- One defender must play with their hands behind their back. This is who the offense should look to target. Change the constrained defender every minute.
- After each score, the offensive players must dribble to the half-court and come back before playing the next defense.
- Different players must initiate the 1-on-1. It is a turnover if the same offensive player tries the 1-on-1 on back-to-back possessions.

### STAFF ROLE

- Count down from 14 seconds.
- Remind players they can only score through 1-on-1 from the perimeter or post.

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "Where is the match-up advantage greatest?"
- "Where should the help defender position themselves to be ready for the drive?"
